Class CurrencyReconciler

java.lang.Object
com.eqixiac.equinix.design.value.CurrencyReconciler
public final class CurrencyReconciler extends Object
The single reconciliation rule shared by every design-time cost model (TcoEngine, SavingsCalculatorEngine, MetroOptimizerEngine, DeploymentWizardEngine, and plan value realization).

Rule: monetary amounts may only be added, subtracted, or compared when they share a currency. This SDK models prices with no FX rate at all — live Fabric pricing for an EMEA metro can quote EUR while the bundled cloud-egress reference figures are USD — so summing across currencies would fabricate a figure that is simply wrong. When components disagree, this helper refuses to produce a combined total and instead exposes the per-currency subtotals and a human-readable reason, so the caller can mark the total unpriced/mixed (mirroring the existing priced/complete guards) rather than emit a false number labelled as authoritative.

Used two ways:

  • as an accumulator (add(Currency, BigDecimal, BigDecimal)) for a stream of priced components that are meant to sum into one deployment total — it tallies per-currency subtotals and yields a combined total only via monthlyTotal()/setupTotal(), which are empty when more than one currency is present;
  • via the static knownDifferent(String, String) / sameKnownCurrency(String, String) predicates at the two-sided subtract/compare sites (egress − interconnect, baseline − recommended, break-even, payback).

The predicates deliberately treat an unknown (null/blank) currency as "not provably different": they block a combination only when two currencies are both known and genuinely differ, so a malformed null currency never silently flips an all-one-currency calculation to unpriced. Absence is tracked separately via sawUnknownCurrency().

Not thread-safe; each computation builds its own instance.

    • monthlyTotal

      public Optional<BigDecimal> monthlyTotal()
      The combined monthly total — present only when the components reconcile to a single currency, empty when they are mixed (a cross-currency sum would be false).

      Empty-reconciler caveat: when nothing priceable was recorded — including when every added component carried a null/blank currency — this returns Optional.of(ZERO), not Optional.empty(): zero is the correct sum of no components, but it is not evidence that anything was priced. Callers must therefore pair this with isEmpty() / sawUnknownCurrency() (as the engines' priced/complete flags do) before presenting the total, or an all-unpriceable accumulation reads as "costs $0" — exactly the fabricated figure this class exists to prevent.

    • setupTotal
